liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Estimated Prophet** (2 reviews): Garcia uses full-on wah pedal, creating a rich, full sound during the performance; Jerry is described as possessed during the twenty-five-minute segment, with unparalled ideas flowing [11][20]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): Song begins with a short Lesh solo, who thumps along noticeably throughout the track [11]
- **Saint Stephen** (1 review): Considered the best version in band history, though the last verses after the jam were skipped [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1977-05-15.mtx.sirmick.91911.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 170 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd1977-05-15.28916.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 181 min; rated 4.79/5 by 56 [2]
- **gd1977-05-15.sbd.bertha.31605.sbeok.flac24**: soundboard; 22 songs; 181 min; rated 5/5 by 8 [3]. Said about its sound: Custom dual-DAW remaster balances mid-bass to avoid obtrusive kick thumping despite good original sound [3]
- **gd1977-05-15.164607.fob.sony.gatto.mckenzie.miller.clugston.flac1644**: audience recording; 22 songs; 184 min [4]
- **gd77-05-15.sbd.gorinsky.7008.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 170 min; rated 3.84/5 by 19 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer describes the mix as fair but the overall sound quality as subpar; Reviewer suggests audience recordings capture the rowdy crowd and bouncing sounds better than board; Recording quality is severely lacking, with significant hiss noted by the reviewer [12][15][16][18][19]

## Around the show

- A terrible cut occurs at 5:58 in the performance of Ship of Fools [12]
- First time Iko Iko was played, with the band on stage start to finish [15]
- Happy Birthday Mick is performed before Ship Of Fools in the second set [4]
- Second set described as otherworldly, though less expansive than other shows from that tour [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1977-05-15.mtx.sirmick.91911.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by SirMick; source: Matrix [1]. Also: First generation cassette transferred by David Minches using Nak Dragon and Grace Lunatec V3 [1]
- **gd1977-05-15.28916.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Transferred and edited by Charlie Miller from DAT via SEK'D Prodif Plus to FLAC [2]
- **gd1977-05-15.sbd.bertha.31605.sbeok.flac24**: transferred by Jay Ashley; source: sbd > mr > dat > wav > flac > daw(Bertha) > wav > audio dvd > dvd audio ripper > wav > adobe audtion > flac [3]
- **gd1977-05-15.164607.fob.sony.gatto.mckenzie.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Keith Gatto; transferred by Tim McKenzie;Charlie Miller;Scott Clugston; source: Keith Gatto's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Sony Stereo mic > Sony TC-158 > PCM (x1) > Tim McKenzies' DAT (x1)(TDK DA-R) [4]
- **gd77-05-15.sbd.gorinsky.7008.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [6]. Also: Reviewer notes cassette in the lineage, preferring a clean soundboard to PCM transfer [10]

## Art and photos

- Poster by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead - 1977-05-15 St. Louis Arena, St. Louis, MO](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2018/10/grateful-dead-1977-05-15-st-louis-arena.html) [23]
- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1977-05-15 Sun St. Louis Arena, St. Louis, MO](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1373008173626/grateful-dead-1977-05-15-sun-st-louis) [24]
- Photo by a Flickr member (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - 5/15/77 St. Louis Arena, St. Louis, MO …](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/27304786131/) [25]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/27304786131/) [26]
